title: Telemetry ownership: metadata profiles, sampling-backed retention and rule-driven redaction
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: telemetry streams (traces, logs, metrics) lack consistent ownership metadata and profile-based handling. This causes accidental long retention of PII-like fields and inconsistent access controls across tenants. Goal: introduce a lightweight metadata profile (ownership, sensitivity, retention-class) attached to telemetry objects, enable sampling-backed retention tiers, and enforce rule-driven redaction prior to long-term storage or cross-tenant export.
background: Several incidents and audits showed: (1) traces occasionally contain user-identifiable tokens from third-party connectors, (2) metrics logs exported for analytics included request paths with PII, (3) access logs are too permissive for low-trust teams. Existing tickets address redaction and retention elsewhere but none provide a unified ownership metadata model paired with sampling/retention mechanics.
goals: Design a metadata profile model: owner, sensitivity (public|internal|sensitive|restricted), retention_class (ephemeral|standard|archival), and allowed_exports
Implement SDK hooks to attach metadata at span/log/metric creation in runtime (go/python/node) and ensure metadata is preserved in pipeline
Introduce a sampling-backed retention controller: high-cardinality sensitive telemetry should be sampled aggressively and short-retained unless elevated
Build rule-driven redaction as a processing stage (configurable regex/field masks + ML-assisted detectors) before long-term storage
Enforce tenant-scoped RBAC on telemetry read/export and log access logging for all privileged views
acceptance_criteria: Metadata profile defined and documented in design doc and console UI spec
Runtime SDKs add metadata without increasing p95 latency by >5% in synthetic load test
Pipeline applies sampling and retention-class correctly for 95% of synthetic test cases
Redaction rules applied with false-positive rate <5% and false-negative rate <2% on evaluation dataset
Audit trail created for any access to restricted telemetry and surfaced in console activity feed
tasks: Write design doc: metadata schema, lifecycle, and ownership model (CONFLUENCE-OBS/Telemetry-Ownership)
Propose console UX for profile creation and default policies
SDK changes: add attach_metadata API and examples in go/python/node
Pipeline: implement sampling-retention controller and pluggable redaction stage
RBAC: add read/export guard and access logging hooks in AuthZ layer
Create end-to-end tests and chaos scenarios that inject PII into traces to validate redaction
Coordinate with security/compliance for policy sign-off and legal for retention windows
risks: SDK adoption friction: library changes required in customer integrations could delay rollout
Performance overhead: redaction and metadata propagation could increase latency unless optimized
False negatives in redaction may leak sensitive data if detectors are misconfigured
Policy complexity: too many retention classes may confuse users and ops
mitigations: Canary rollout with runtime flag and telemetry sampling off by default; provide migration guide
Implement redaction as asynchronous post-commit transform for archival tier to avoid p99 impact
Create an evaluation harness and labeled dataset drawn from prior incidents to tune detectors
Limit initial release to 3 retention classes and expand after UX research
